newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES FIRMER IN ACTIVE TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES FIRMER IN ACTIVE TRADE.

text.p: Short term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market edged up on Monday despite liquidity in the system, largely tracking a firmer treasury bill rate after last Friday's correction move by the central Reserve Bank, dealers said.

On Friday afternoon, the central bank issued a statement that the treasury bill rate would revert back to its previous levels after it dropped drastically at Thursday's weekly tender following an error made by one discount house in placing its tender price.
The error had rendered most market players reluctant to trade at the low rates for fear of making losses.
But on Monday morning most houses said business was back to normal and they were doing brisk trade.
"There are a lot of maturities today and a lot of trade in treasury bills," a dealer said.
Discount houses were buying 91-day treasury bills at 19.36 percent, up from 15.44 percent and selling them back into the market at 19 percent.
NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days edged up to 21 percent from 20 and bankers acceptances were also firmer at 19.50 percent from 19.25.
Call money, which tumbled to a zero to 15 percentage range after the error, was on Monday quoted at 18 percent in a market which opened with a Z$33 million surplus.
